note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — TRUE LIGULE, THEN PLUME
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1322) — At the inner blade–sheath junction, look for a stiff membrane. The Flora gives 2–5 mm and describes a loosely contracted, yellowish panicle.

The rifle-sight outline includes pointed SHEATH CORNERS beside the actual free membrane. Do not call the green corners the ligule or identify from fall color. Existing Matt Lavin source photograph shows the true membrane; the USGS comparison angle illustrates sheath corners, but neither supplies a measured same-plant 1-mm ruler. Flowering panicle is elongated and branched, not big bluestem's exposed turkey-foot fingers. 2026 LOCAL KYLE photos added: panel 9 is an in-ground clump and panel 10 is a pale collar point. Neither proves belowground rhizomes or a measured free ligule.
tiles.short: Open the blade–sheath junction: upright pale 2–6 mm membranous ligule; then find ONE branched golden panicle.
tiles.status: TRUE COLLAR PHOTO PRESENT — MEASURED SAME-PLANT COLLAR STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · GROWTH FORM / NODES / COLLAR
tiles.details: Inspect the actual crown and short rhizomes on a connected specimen; a seedhead-only image cannot prove rhizomes. Culms can be tall and nodes hairy, but neither stature nor hair is decisive. Iowa treatment gives a broader 1.5–7 mm ligule range; measure the membrane alone, not its flanking sheath projections. A complete rooted Hays-area flowering specimen and exposed basal crown are not yet photographed together.
tiles.short: Warm-season tufted perennial with short scaly rhizomes; true membranous ligule usually ~2–6 mm.
tiles.status: PUBLISHED GROWTH FORM — ROOTED CROWN AND MM SCALE MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · SESSILE SPIKELET, GLUMES AND NAKED PEDICEL
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1322) — Measure the spikelet body. The Flora gives a usual length of 6–8 mm.

The source-authenticated Matt Lavin macro actually shows an awned sessile spikelet and bare pedicel; it is not a second fully developed spikelet. Under 10–20× separate the enclosing glumes: Iowa treatment describes both ~5–8 mm, lower commonly 7–9-veined and hairy, upper about 5-veined and relatively smooth; AusGrass describes upper 5–7 veins. A reduced lower sterile floret may occur INSIDE the fertile spikelet, so 'one fertile floret' does not mean only one lemma. Published ranges are not measured from gallery pixels.
tiles.short: Fertile spikelet usually 5–8 mm, with one fertile floret; paired sterile partner is reduced to a NAKED hairy pedicel.
tiles.status: REAL REPRODUCTIVE MACRO — GLUME DISSECTION WITH 1-MM SCALE MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · FERTILE LEMMA AND ITS BENT AWN
tiles.details: AusGrass describes a thin three-nerved fertile lemma with two narrow apical lobes and a central geniculate awn, commonly 10–22 mm; Iowa reports (6–)8–17 mm, while Go Botany gives 10–30 mm. These treatment ranges differ and overlap S. elliottii: never impose a rigid awn cutoff. Separate the lower sterile lemma (~4–6 mm in AusGrass) from the fertile awned lemma and two outer glumes before placing organ-specific arrows. The current macro lacks a millimeter scale and independently resolved lemma insertion.
tiles.short: Fertile lemma ~3–5.5 mm; a single bent/twisted awn arises from its notched tip, NOT from the naked pedicel.
tiles.status: PUBLISHED DISSECTION ANATOMY — NO UNVERIFIED FINE ARROWS

tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Sorghastrum nutans has a true membranous rifle-sight collar, one elongated branched plume and a fertile sessile spikelet with bare sterile pedicel. Big bluestem has a few stout terminal racemes; little bluestem many short silky racemes; bushy bluestem a dense brushy spathe-bracted crown. Slender Indiangrass (S. elliottii) may have a more one-sided arching panicle, no spreading rhizomes and usually longer twice-bent awns, but lengths overlap. Existing slender comparison panels are source-determined OTHER-SPECIES provisional photos; do not certify that species or Hays nativity from these images.
tiles.short: Big bluestem = terminal fingers; switchgrass = diffuse open panicle; Johnsongrass = developed pedicelled partner.
tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE GALLERY PRESENT — MATCHED VOUCHER/MEASURED SPLIT MISSING

tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / PHOTO AND SITE HANDOFF
tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: rooted Hays-area plant with exposed short rhizomes and attached entire flowering panicle; opened true ligule plus distinct sheath corners at 1-mm scale; one attached mature sessile spikelet with naked pedicel and separated glumes, sterile lemma, fertile lemma and complete awn beside 1-mm scale; at least three measured intact awns; vouchered S. elliottii comparison at same scale. NEEDS_SITE_QA: check all eight existing gallery panels and other-species labels, two remote-only Commons images, the federal external collar angle, five stored records including PRIVATE-ONLY Joey video frame, CC BY-NC Joey stills, CC BY-SA Matt Lavin photos, source attribution, EXIF/GPS, mobile tile indices and arrow placement. Do not expose private frame, invent arrows, claim deployment or clear S. elliottii holds.
tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: seven existing image records, five locally stored; no same-plant calibrated collar/awn series.

steps.title: Local Kyle · Recognize the standing bunch
steps.look_for: Observe this actual growing indiangrass clump photographed in Kyle, including the long green basal leaves and the shoot bases at ground level. The true belowground roots are NOT visible.
steps.why_it_matters: Teaches the crew what the plant actually looks like locally without implying the photo proves its underground rhizomes.

steps.title: 1 · Locate the collar and pointed projection
steps.look_for: See a tall narrow pointed collar projection and the pale inner blade–sheath junction on a real source-identified photograph. The true 2–6 mm free ligule is NOT measurably separated.
steps.why_it_matters: Beginners often confuse the green sheath corners with the free ligule. The arrows show the physical location but don't establish millimeter length.

steps.title: Local Kyle · Find the narrow leaf collar
steps.look_for: John Davis photographed a pale collar point beside the green blade and sheath. Check the same feature in Matt Lavin macro; no ruler proves membrane length.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects accurate Texas field context to anatomy without labeling a green sheath point as a measured free ligule.

steps.title: 2 · Recognize the whole flowering habit
steps.look_for: Follow a flowering culm upward to a single elongated, branching plume. The base and actual short rhizomes are not exposed in this distant reference image.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit helps decide where to look next; color alone cannot distinguish grasses.

steps.title: 3 · Follow branches inside the golden seedhead
steps.look_for: Look for many branches within one terminal branched panicle, rather than several stout, exposed turkey-foot fingers.
steps.why_it_matters: This separates indiangrass's overall flowering architecture from big bluestem.

steps.title: 4 · Recognize a fertile spikelet and bent awn
steps.look_for: Find the golden elongated spikelet body and a much longer dark twisted/bent awn, distinct from the many fine hairs.
steps.why_it_matters: The bent awn and spikelet are real visible parts; the tiny naked sterile pedicel and awn insertion are not confidently isolated by arrows here.

steps.title: 5 · Compare actual big bluestem
steps.look_for: The reference is a DIFFERENT species, big bluestem, with exposed terminal turkey-foot-type racemes; compare branching architecture with indiangrass.
steps.why_it_matters: Don't remove a suspected native species based on golden color, height or a fragmentary seedhead.

steps.title: 6 · Check slender indiangrass carefully
steps.look_for: Slender indiangrass can have a more curved head and longer, often twice-bent awns, but this comparison photo is source-determined and not a measured voucher.
steps.why_it_matters: Keep uncertain Sorghastrum as genus pending multiple intact awns and a real collar/rootstock comparison.

intro: Learn real indiangrass with source-credited botanical photos. First find the blade–sheath collar, then the branched golden panicle and the awned fertile spikelet. The collar photo has a pointed projection, but neither it nor the pale tissue is a measured free membrane; use a ruler and an opened sheath for final confirmation.
memory_rule: Leaf collar (rifle-sight tendency) + single golden branched panicle + bent awn on fertile spikelet. Big bluestem = turkey-foot fingers; switchgrass = diffuse, hair-ligule panicle.
safety_note: Indiangrass is recorded in the Hays/Travis/Williamson target-zone audit. This guide uses actual sources, but no Hays plant with whole connected roots, an opened calibrated ligule and measured mature spikelet/pedicel pair has yet been archived. Scientific S. elliottii determination/range remains held.
field_rule: RIFLE-SIGHT MEMBRANE + SINGLE GOLDEN BRANCHED HEAD + AWNED SPIKELET/BARE PEDICEL.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
comparison_text: Sorghastrum nutans: conspicuous upright membranous rifle-sight-like ligule and a single branched panicle with awned fertile spikelets and reduced pedicelled partners. Big bluestem: open digitate turkey-foot. Bushy bluestem: dense spathe-bracted brush. Little bluestem: many short silky racemes on upper branchlets. S. elliottii requires measured awns and collars before a firm split; do not apply a rigid length cutoff.
